LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains standard variable assignments and a `source` array pointing to the expected upstream release tarball over HTTPS. The `sha256sums` array includes a valid checksum, indicating the source integrity is verified. There are no command substitutions, function calls, or executable statements in the global scope — only declarative metadata. Sourcing this file during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will not trigger any network activity, data exfiltration, or code execution. All functions (`build`, `check`, `package`) are out of scope for this phase, as they are not executed during `--printsrcinfo`. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and presents no immediate risk when sourced.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>No executable code in global scope</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD follows standard Arch Linux packaging practices. It defines clear metadata, depends on legitimate libraries, and retrieves the source from the official project URL over HTTPS. The source integrity is verified using a matching SHA-256 checksum. The build process uses standard autotools workflow (`autogen.sh`, `make`, `make install`) without obfuscation or unusual commands. The `check()` function runs tests with `make check -k`, which is a normal quality assurance step. There are no network operations during build or package phases beyond the initial source download, no use of `eval`, `curl|bash`, or base64 decoding, and no file operations outside the build directory or `$pkgdir`. All actions are confined to building and installing the declared software.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
Standard packaging, no malicious behavior detected</summary>
</security_assessment>

[1/2] Reviewing .SRCINFO...
+ Reviewed PKGBUILD. Status: SAFE -- Standard packaging, no malicious behavior detected
LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package build configuration. It lists the package name, version, dependencies, source URL, and checksum. The source is a tarball from the official project domain `gnomevoice.org`, which aligns with the package's stated purpose. The `sha256sums` entry provides a valid cryptographic hash for the source, ensuring integrity. There are no scripts, commands, or executable content in this file—only declarative package metadata. The listed dependencies are standard GNOME and GStreamer libraries, consistent with a GNOME audio application. No network operations, file manipulations, or system modifications are present or implied in this file. As such, there is no evidence of malicious behavior.
</details>
